Perfect! I've successfully found and read all the key Next.js App Router migration and reference documentation. Let me provide you with a comprehensive summary of the available docs and the key information about App Router structure. ## Available Documentation Files The Next.js App Router docs are located in `/vercel/sandbox/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/`. Here's what's available: **Getting Started Docs:** - Installation guide - Project structure and organization - Layouts and pages - Linking and navigating - Server and client components - Data fetching - Error handling - CSS, images, fonts, metadata **API Reference - File Conventions:** - `layout.mdx` - Layout files - `page.mdx` - Page files - `route.mdx` - Route handlers (API routes) - `loading.mdx` - Loading UI - `error.mdx` - Error boundaries - `dynamic-routes.mdx` - Dynamic routing - And metadata files (icons, sitemap, robots, etc.) **Migration Guides:** - `app-router-migration.mdx` - Complete migration guide from Pages Router to App Router --- ## Key Information About App Router Structure ### 1. File-Based Routing with File-System Organization The App Router uses **folders to define URL segments** and **special files** to define UI: - **`page.js`** - Renders UI unique to a route (required to make a route public) - **`layout.js`** - Shared UI across multiple routes (nested and cacheable) - **`route.js`** - API endpoints (Route Handlers) - **Folders** - Define URL segments in the path ### 2. Creating Pages Pages are Server Components by default: ```tsx // app/page.tsx - Home page at / export default function Page() { return

Hello Next.js!

} // app/blog/page.tsx - Creates /blog route export default function BlogPage() { return

Blog

} // app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx - Dynamic route for /blog/post-1 export default async function BlogPostPage({ params }) { const { slug } = await params return

{slug}

} ``` ### 3. Creating Layouts Layouts accept a `children` prop and are shared across multiple routes. They preserve state and don't re-render on navigation: ```tsx // app/layout.tsx - Root layout (REQUIRED) export default function RootLayout({ children }) { return ( {children} ) } // app/blog/layout.tsx - Nested layout for blog routes export default function BlogLayout({ children }) { return
{children}
} ``` **Key Points:** - The **root layout** must define `` and `` tags - Layouts are cached client-side during navigation - Layouts can access `params` (dynamic route parameters) - Multiple root layouts can be created using route groups like `(shop)` and `(marketing)` ### 4. Route Handlers (API Routes) Route Handlers replace Pages Router API routes. They use Web Request/Response APIs: ```tsx // app/api/route.ts - Handles GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS export async function GET(request: NextRequest) { return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' }) } export async function POST(request: NextRequest) { const data = await request.json() return Response.json({ data }) } // app/api/items/[slug]/route.ts - Dynamic route handlers export async function GET(request, { params }) { const { slug } = await params return Response.json({ slug }) } ``` **Key Points:** - Cannot coexist with `page.js` at the same route level - By default, GET is not cached (changed in v15) - Support dynamic segments, headers, cookies, URL params, streaming - Use `NextRequest` and `NextResponse` for extended APIs ### 5. Dynamic Routes Use square brackets to create dynamic segments: ``` app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx → /blog/post-1 app/shop/[...slug]/page.tsx → /shop/clothing/shirts (catch-all) app/docs/[[...slug]]/page.tsx → /docs, /docs/api/reference (optional catch-all) ``` Access dynamic parameters via the `params` prop: ```tsx export default async function Page({ params }) { const { slug } = await params } ``` ### 6. Nested Routes and Hierarchy Routes are defined by folder nesting: ``` app/ layout.tsx (Root layout for all routes) page.tsx (Home page /) blog/ layout.tsx (Layout for /blog and descendants) page.tsx (Blog index /blog) [slug]/ page.tsx (Individual posts /blog/[slug]) dashboard/ layout.tsx (Dashboard layout) page.tsx (/dashboard) ``` ### 7. Migration from Pages Router Key mapping: | Pages Router | App Router | Notes | |---|---|---| | `pages/_app.js` | `app/layout.js` | Root layout replaces _app | | `pages/_document.js` | `app/layout.js` | Root layout replaces _document | | `pages/404.js` | `app/not-found.js` | Not found page | | `pages/_error.js` | `app/error.js` | Error boundaries | | `pages/api/*` | `app/api/*/route.js` | Route Handlers | | `getServerSideProps` | `fetch(..., { cache: 'no-store' })` | Server-side rendering | | `getStaticProps` | `fetch(..., { cache: 'force-cache' })` | Static generation | | `getStaticPaths` | `generateStaticParams()` | Pre-render dynamic routes | ### 8. Data Fetching Use `async/await` directly in Server Components: ```tsx // Similar to getServerSideProps (re-fetch on every request) const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'no-store' }) // Similar to getStaticProps (cache until revalidated) const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'force-cache' }) // With ISR (cache for 10 seconds) const data = await fetch('https://...', { next: { revalidate: 10 } }) ``` ### 9. Special Features - **Route Groups**: Use parentheses `(marketing)` to organize without affecting URLs - **Private Folders**: Use underscore `_components` to opt out of routing - **Search Parameters**: Use `searchParams` prop in pages - **Metadata API**: Use `export const metadata = {...}` instead of `next/head` - **Server vs Client Components**: Pages are Server Components by default; add `'use client'` for Client Components All these features are documented in detail in the files located at `/vercel/sandbox/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/`.

events.content:
The migration is complete. Here's a summary of what was done:

### Changes Made

**Created:**
- `app/layout.tsx` — Root layout with `<html>` and `<body>` tags, replacing both `pages/_app.tsx` and `pages/_document.tsx`. Metadata (title, description, favicon) is handled via the `export const metadata` API instead of `next/head`.
- `app/page.tsx` — Home page as a Server Component, preserving the same UI (heading, welcome text, nav links).

**Removed:**
- `pages/_app.tsx` — No longer needed; the root layout handles app-level wrapping.
- `pages/_document.tsx` — No longer needed; the root layout defines the HTML structure.
- `pages/index.tsx` — Replaced by `app/page.tsx`.

### Key Migration Patterns Applied
- **`next/head` → Metadata API**: The `<Head>` component with `<title>`, `<meta>`, and `<link>` tags was replaced with the `export const metadata` object in the layout.
- **`_app.tsx` + `_document.tsx` → `layout.tsx`**: Both files are consolidated into a single root layout that defines the HTML shell and wraps all pages.
- **Pages are Server Components by default**: No `'use client'` directive needed since the page has no client-side interactivity.

The build completes successfully with the route `○ /` statically prerendered.
